name: One-pot chicken breast & spelt pasta (tomato)
balance_rule: ~37 g dry spelt pasta per 100 g raw chicken → ~1:1 protein:carb (optimal balance); at higher chicken weights it drifts up slightly (~39 g/100 g) because the fixed base is constant. Use ~31 g/100 g for a protein-forward cut. This logged batch used 295 g pasta / 870 g chicken (~34 g/100 g, protein-forward at 1.11:1).

logged_instance.note: User's chosen ratio — protein-forward (1.11:1 protein:carb). Oil measured at 20 g this batch (leaner than the ~35 g template default), which drops per-serving fat. Prior batch was 640 g chicken / 200 g pasta.

source.author: User's recurring one-pot dish
source.notes: Parametric template. Fixed base is constant; chicken and spelt pasta are input per batch. Same dish family as the foods.json 'chicken-pasta bake'. 'Spoon' read as tablespoon. Olive oil template default ~2.5 tbsp (~35 g), but the user has since measured it at 20 g — use 20 g going forward. Per-serving values below reflect the current logged batch split into 5.

serving_desc: ≈310 g (batch ÷5). This batch: 870 g raw chicken + 295 g dry spelt pasta + 20 g olive oil
steps: Coat the chicken breast in beaten egg + cornflour.
Sear the chicken in generous olive oil.
Add cherry tomatoes, Mutti tomato paste, salt and 0.5 tsp sugar; cook down to a sauce.
Add the cooked/cooking spelt pasta and combine in the one pot.

him.verdict: A near-ideal cutting + muscle-retention meal. ~37% of calories from protein (45 g/serving), protein-forward 1.13:1 protein:carb, lean chicken, whole-grain spelt fiber, and a real sperm-micro hit — lycopene from the tomatoes + Mutti paste, plus selenium and zinc from the chicken/spelt. The only calorie lever worth watching is the 'generous' olive oil.
suggested_mods: Measure the olive oil (~1.5–2 tbsp is plenty) — it's the main swing factor in the calorie count
Toss in spinach or serve over greens to add folate the dish is a little short on
Bump to ~240 g pasta if you want a clean 1:1 balance / a more filling day

her_preconception.verdict: Strong preconception dish. Lean protein + choline (~139 mg/serving from chicken + egg), iron naturally paired with the tomatoes' vitamin C for better absorption, plus lycopene and selenium. Everything is fully cooked (egg coating and chicken), so no safety flags. Folate is the one gap — easily closed with greens.
prenatal_highlights: iron paired with tomato vitamin C (better non-heme absorption)
lycopene + selenium from tomatoes/paste and chicken
suggested_mods: Add a couple of handfuls of spinach for folate + extra iron
Spelt contains gluten — fine unless she's avoiding it

adopted_note: Promoted to the daily rotation 2026-08-09. Template: macros change with the chicken & pasta weights input each batch — use the balance_rule (~37 g dry spelt per 100 g raw chicken for 1:1; ~31 g/100 g protein-forward). Per-100g values are what to reuse when logging a day.
cooking_guide: Boil the spelt pasta in well-salted water to just under al dente (it finishes in the sauce); scoop out a cup of pasta water before draining.
Pat the chicken strips dry, then coat in beaten egg + cornflour — the dry surface and starch give a light crust that keeps the chicken juicy.
Sear the chicken in the olive oil over medium-high, undisturbed, until golden and just cooked (74 C); remove and set aside so it doesn't overcook.
In the same pot, cook the cherry tomatoes and tomato paste with a pinch of salt and the 1/2 tsp sugar 5-8 min until jammy — the sugar balances the tomato acidity.
Loosen the sauce with a splash of pasta water, then fold in the pasta and chicken and toss 1-2 min so the pasta drinks up the flavor.
Taste, adjust salt and pepper, finish with fresh herbs.
Tip: measure the olive oil (~20 g) — it's the single biggest calorie swing in the dish.
